chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah Mighty and Majestic revealed to Dawood (peace be upon him): 'A servant from My servants comes to Me with a good deed, so I grant him My Paradise.' Dawood (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, and what is that good deed?' He said: 'Causing gladness to enter upon My believing servant, even if it be by giving a date.' Dawood (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, it is true for the one who knows You that he does not cut off his hope from You.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific good deed that causes Allah to grant His Paradise, according to the revelation to Prophet Dawood?
ai.summary: In this Hadith Qudsi from al-Kafi, Allah reveals to Prophet Dawood that the reward for Paradise can be earned by a single act of bringing joy to a believer, even as simple as giving a date. This highlights the immense spiritual weight of 'Faraj al-Kariba' (relieving distress) in Shia tradition, emphasizing that social kindness is a direct path to divine proximity. The narration concludes with Dawood’s affirmation that true gnosis of God sustains unbroken hope, linking theological knowledge with practical compassion.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto Dawood<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>: “The servant from My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> servants, let him come to Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> with the good deeds, so I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> can Gift My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Paradise to him”. So Dawood<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! And what is that deed?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Said: “Causing the gladness to enter upon My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> believeing servant, and even if it be by a date”. Dawood<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! It is true for the one who recognises You<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> that he would not cut off his hopes from You<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>’’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

‘‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, sent revelations to David that said, ‘One of my servants may come to Me with a good deed and I admit him in paradise.’ David asked, ‘Lord, what is that good deed?’ The Lord said, ‘It is bringing joy to the heart of my believing servant even if it is by one piece of date.’ David then said, ‘Lord, it is very true that one who comes to know You must not lose hope of Your kindness.’”
